intro: Before you stands the Temple of Zeus at Aizanoi, from AD 92 - 95, the best-preserved temple of Zeus in Anatolia. It is a pseudodipteros of eight by fifteen columns, raised over a vaulted chamber lit by windows. It was dedicated under Domitian, and most of its columns are still standing.
spot-1: Now you are looking at a corner column. The temple has eight columns by fifteen; share the corners, and you count forty-two in all.
spot-2: Now you are looking at the pronaos, the deep porch in front of the cella. From here, the door opened inwards.
spot-3: Now you are looking at the cella, the closed chamber that once held the cult statue of Zeus.
spot-4: Now you are looking at what makes this a pseudodipteros. Notice the gap between the colonnade and the cella: it is left one ring wide.
spot-5: Now you are looking at the place of the vaulted chamber. A barrel vault lit by windows runs beneath the temple, probably a cult room. It is not modelled; this marker only shows where it lies.
uncertainty: Finally, what this model does not know. The stylobate dimensions and the column counts on the sides come from the English Wikipedia, and the total of 42 columns follows from them. The column height (9 m), the diameter, the entablature, the roof and the cella walls are not measured but proportioned from the Ionic order. In the pseudodipteral plan, the place of the second ring of columns is left empty and the cella is set back by that much. The vaulted chamber beneath the temple and its light windows are not modelled, and the podium is shown only as a stepped crepis.
